Layers:
  continuous: aspect_deg (Direction the ground faces, i.e. the compass bearing of steepest DESCENT, degrees clockwise from north (0 = faces north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west), Horn 3x3 finite difference on the 2 m elevation (about 6 m support), same gradient as slope_2m. 'North-facing' means aspect_deg within 45 deg of 0 (or aspect_class N / NE / NW)); curvature_plan (Curvature of the contour line across the slope (spurs / ridges diverge = positive, gullies / hollows converge = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Sign convention (both layers): POSITIVE = convex (crest, spur, dome), NEGATIVE = concave (hollow, valley, bowl); values are 1/m, so a paraboloid z = a r^2 gives -2a. (Zevenbergen and Thorne's raw plan-curvature formula has the opposite sign to their profile formula; plan is flipped here so both read the same way.) ); curvature_profile (Curvature of the surface along the downslope direction (convex breaks of slope at the top of scarps = positive, concave bases = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Counts layers, not independent minerals: mixed prototypes appear in more than one layer, and pyroxene/smectite variants count separately); outcrop_exposure (Height proxy for an exposed vertical section: local_relief_50m where at least 2% of the cells within 50 m have slope_2m >= 25 degrees (a steep face is actually present in the window), else 0.
